scenario.title: 鄰居太吵、室友的壞習慣
scenario.context: 抱怨別人的壞習慣時，英文有一個很特別的用法：always + 現在進行式。He's always leaving his dishes in the sink 不只是描述事實，還帶著「煩死了」的情緒，這是母語者抱怨時最常用的句型。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: My upstairs neighbor is driving me up the wall.
lines.zh: 我樓上的鄰居快把我逼瘋了。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: He's always moving furniture at 2 a.m. And his dog is constantly barking.
lines.zh: 他老是在凌晨兩點搬家具，而且他的狗一直在叫。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: That would get on my nerves too. Have you talked to him?
lines.zh: 我也會受不了。你跟他談過嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Not yet. I'm worried he'll get defensive.
lines.zh: 還沒，我怕他會防衛心很重。

lines.speaker: Jess
lines.en: You could leave a friendly note first. Something like "Hi, just a heads-up about the noise."
lines.zh: 你可以先留張友善的紙條，像是「嗨，想提醒一下噪音的事」。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Good idea. That feels less confrontational.
lines.zh: 好主意，那樣感覺比較不會正面衝突。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: Hi, I'm Minz from 4F. Sorry to bother you. Do you have a minute?
lines.zh: 嗨，我是四樓的 Minz，抱歉打擾。你有空一下嗎？

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: I just wanted to mention that it gets pretty loud late at night. I can hear furniture moving around 2 a.m.
lines.zh: 我只是想提一下，晚上蠻吵的，我凌晨兩點左右會聽到搬家具的聲音。

lines.speaker: Neighbor
lines.en: Oh no, I'm so sorry. I work night shifts, and I didn't realize the noise traveled.
lines.zh: 喔不，真的很抱歉。我上夜班，沒想到聲音會傳下去。

lines.speaker: Minz
lines.en: No worries. Maybe some felt pads under the chairs would help?
lines.zh: 沒關係。也許在椅腳貼防滑墊會有幫助？

lines.speaker: Neighbor
lines.en: Great idea. I'll get some this weekend. Thanks for telling me nicely.
lines.zh: 好主意，我這週末去買。謝謝你這麼客氣地告訴我。

patterns.en: It gets pretty loud at night.
Would you mind keeping it down after 11?
patterns.zh: 十一點後可以小聲一點嗎？

patterns.en: I don't want to cause any trouble.
Maybe we could find a solution.
patterns.zh: 也許我們可以找個解決辦法。

patterns.en: I'll talk to the building manager.

chinglish.right: It gets pretty loud. / The noise is really loud.
chinglish.why: 「聲音很大」直翻 big 不對，噪音用 loud。另外直接說 your noise 帶指責。

chinglish.wrong: He always leaves dishes, very annoying.
chinglish.right: He's always leaving his dishes in the sink. It's so annoying.
chinglish.why: 抱怨用 always + 進行式最有情緒；後半句要有主詞動詞。

chinglish.right: Would you mind keeping it down a bit?
chinglish.why: 語序不自然。keep it down = 小聲一點，是固定用法。
說 you make me… 容易讓對方防衛。描述情況的感受比較不會起衝突。

grammar.title: always＋進行式表不滿
grammar.oneLiner: be + always / constantly / forever + V-ing：抱怨某人的壞習慣，比簡單式多了「煩死了」的情緒。
whenToUse: 現在：He's always leaving his socks on the floor.（抱怨）
對比：He always leaves at 6.（中性描述習慣）
常用副詞：always, constantly, forever, continually。
過去：She was always interrupting me.
也可以用在正面的驚喜：She's always bringing us snacks!（她老是帶零食來，好可愛）
搭配其他抱怨句型：It drives me crazy when… / I can't stand it when…
grammar.whyWeGetItWrong: 第 1 單元學過：習慣用簡單式，暫時的狀態用進行式。現在這個規則有個例外：always + 進行式反而是在講習慣，而且帶情緒。中文的「老是」「一天到晚」有同樣的效果，但動詞不變。台灣人抱怨時常用簡單式，聽起來像在陳述事實，少了情緒。

examples.correct: My roommate is always borrowing my stuff without asking.
examples.note: 抱怨，帶情緒。always 放在 be 動詞後面。
examples.incorrect: My roommate always is borrowing my stuff without asking.

examples.correct: My roommate always borrows my charger.
He's constantly checking his phone during meetings.
My last boss was forever changing his mind.
Grandma is always sending us food. She's the best.

quiz.question: Which sounds like a complaint?
options: He's always leaving his trash in the hallway.
quiz.explanation: always + 進行式帶抱怨情緒。

quiz.question: My neighbor is ___ playing loud music. (老是)
She ___ interrupting me when I was talking.
Could you keep it ___ after 11 p.m.?
quiz.explanation: keep it down = 小聲一點。

slang.usage: 形容某件事讓人非常煩躁。

examples.en: The construction noise is driving me up the wall.
examples.zh: 工地噪音快把我逼瘋了。

examples.en: His constant humming drives me up the wall.

slang.usage: get on someone's nerves = 讓某人不耐煩。

risk.note: 當面說 You're getting on my nerves 很不客氣。

examples.en: That song is really getting on my nerves.
Little things get on my nerves when I'm tired.
examples.zh: 我累的時候小事都會讓我很煩。

slang.usage: 要對方停止某個煩人的行為，常用在朋友、家人、小孩之間。

risk.note: 語氣直接，對不熟的人或長輩說很失禮。

examples.en: Cut it out, you two! I'm trying to work.
examples.zh: 你們兩個夠了！我在工作。

examples.en: Stop teasing me. Cut it out!

slang.usage: 和 cut it out 類似，語氣更強硬。

risk.note: 語氣很衝，工作場合或對不熟的人不要用。

examples.en: Knock it off! You're going to break something.
I told him to knock it off, but he kept going.
examples.zh: 我叫他別再這樣了，但他還是繼續。

review.question: Feel free ___ use the washing machine.
review.explanation: 複習第 77 單元：feel free to + V。

review.question: A: I can't sleep with all this noise. B: ___
review.explanation: 複習第 76 單元：否定句附和用 neither。

review.question: I'm ___ exhausted. The dog barked all night.
review.explanation: 複習第 74 單元：極端形容詞用 totally。

review.question: If I had known about the noise, I ___ this apartment.
There's a ___ construction project next door.
review.explanation: 複習第 62 單元：複合形容詞。

review.question: The noise stopped. He ___ fallen asleep.
review.explanation: 複習第 46 單元：推測過去。

review.question: I can't stand ___ to loud music at night.
review.explanation: 複習第 14 單元：can't stand + V-ing。

review.question: Which is a complaint?
options: She's always calling me at midnight!
